transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Marco Ruiz (Redwood) -- Dana Chen, Miguel Santos, Priyanka Patel, Rajiv Kapoor (AquilaHealth)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync. Focused on confirming why 95th pct latency still above incumbent, proposed routing and quantization experiments, agreed next steps.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone uh thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, uh quick agenda — recap last week's runs, dig into the 95th pct delta, decide experiments, and next steps.
[00:18] Dana Chen: thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we ran your last suite overnight, saw similar medians but spikes at tails.
[00:27] Priya Nair: yeah, median's looking good, this is the part we wanna nail down — the 95/99 behavior, suspect routing fallback and cold KV cash is factoring in.
[00:40] Miguel Santos: KV cash? you mean KV cache — yeah we saw cache misses during burst windows, that produced big token stall. transcription sometimes shows "KV cash" in logs lol.
[00:52] Jordan Lee: sorry, my bad, yeah KV cache. quick note: our test earlier used auto-batching with a max batch of 32, with a prefer-latency policy.
[01:05] Priya Nair: and we tried two model variants: rwd-7b-fp16 and rwd-7b-q4f, q4f was about 12% cheaper but added jitter on long contexts.
[01:18] Rajiv Kapoor: so why is jitter worse on quantised? shouldnt quantize help throughput?
[01:25] Priya Nair: in general yes for throughput, but for tails quantization plus kernel switching cause some overhead on certain GPUs, also the compile-kernel path sometimes triggers on sequence-length variation. we sometimes see a micro-compile that adds ~30-60ms.
[01:40] Priyanka Patel: are those micro-compiles repeatable? can we pre-jit them?
[01:46] Priya Nair: good question — we can pin a kernel profile or run a warm-up sweep to pre-cache kernels; also prefix/KV prewarm can help.
[01:58] Miguel Santos: baseline IncumbentAI reports 95th at ~220ms on our 1k tokens workload, we're seeing Redwood at ~270-280ms on same replay, medians match ~140ms though.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: ok thanks for the numbers. the gap is real. two candidates: routing fallback (requests being routed to a cheaper but higher-latency variant) or cache misses during load shaping.
[02:26] Dana Chen: about routing — in your description you have cost-tier fallback. can we force latency-first routing for this test?
[02:34] Priya Nair: yes, we can pin policy to latency-first and also pin model version for the test. we'll run three configs: latency-first/pinned, cost-first/with-fallback, and latency-first + KV prewarm.
[02:49] Marco Ruiz: and we'll capture per-token breakdown, queue time, kernel compile time as separate columns in the CSV.
[02:58] Miguel Santos: perfect. also we'll send the 2k prompt set after the call — should be representative.
[03:05] Rajiv Kapoor: on security, quick item: we need to see SOC2 + KMS integration notes before moving to Dedicated. is Redwood's Private option available for our on-prem regs?
[03:16] Jordan Lee: yes, Redwood Private is available — we provide a private control plane and can integrate customer KMS/HSM. we have a SOC2 package we'll share.
[03:24] Priyanka Patel: any difference in latency when on Private vs Hosted?
[03:28] Priya Nair: network topology can add few ms depending on VPC peering, but compute path is same. our Dedicated slots are identical compute unless you choose on-prem hardware.
[03:38] Dana Chen: ok good. back to the bench — what's the plan for quantization? is the q4f variant our recommended production path?
[03:46] Priya Nair: q4f is recommended for heavy throughput with modest quality tradeoff; for tails we might keep fp16 on latency-critical routes. one pattern: use q4f for background batch jobs and fp16 for interactive low-latency calls.
[04:00] Miguel Santos: hmmm interesting. how big of a delta did you see in our runs between q4f and fp16 on 95th?
[04:07] Priya Nair: in the overnight run q4f 95th was ~300-320ms, fp16 95th ~270-280ms — but that included a cold-cache period. after warmup q4f narrowed to ~290.
[04:21] Jordan Lee: right — which aligns with the micro-compile explanation. we suspect a few percent of requests still hit the compile path.
[04:30] Dana Chen: is there telemetry we can add to detect compile hits?
[04:34] Priya Nair: yes, we'll include kernel-compile-duration in traces, and a flag for "cache_hit" for KV.
[04:42] Marco Ruiz: also adding request_hop_count so we can see if some requests got routed through fallback regions.
[04:50] Miguel Santos: during a small spike yesterday, CPU was also high on the gateway — could that be queueing at the frontend?
[04:57] Priya Nair: precise — we log frontend queue time. if gateway CPU saturates you'll see elevated queue and that hurts tails even if GPU is fine.
[05:08] Rajiv Kapoor: do you recommend Dedicated slot for our workload to avoid gateway variance?
[05:13] Jordan Lee: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor at the serving tier but some gateway functions remain shared unless you opt for private egress. we can offer Dedicated + private egress for stricter isolation.
[05:26] Dana Chen: cost impact?
[05:28] Jordan Lee: I'll share detailed pricing; rough ballpark, Dedicated slot plus burst is about X% above hosted for our compute region — I'll send exact numbers.
[05:37] Miguel Santos: can we run a head-to-head with IncumbentAI in the same replay environment? we ran offline but want the live compare under identical traffic shaping.
[05:46] Priya Nair: yes, we can set up mirrored replay so both endpoints receive same traffic. caveat: IncumbentAI requires their tokenization differences to be accounted for but we can normalize at the prompt level.
[05:58] Priyanka Patel: what about batching? you said max batch 32 — does changing batch windows help tails?
[06:04] Priya Nair: increasing max batch increases throughput but can add latency if the batching window waits for fill. we can lower batching wait-time for latency-sensitive routes so they don't wait. it's a tradeoff.
[06:16] Jordan Lee: suggestion: for the test, set batch_wait_ms to 5ms for latency-first route and 30ms for cost-first route. compare 95th across both.
[06:25] Miguel Santos: agreed. also include a run with KV disabled to quantify impact.
[06:29] Priya Nair: yep, that'll isolate cache benefits.
[06:33] -- mid-call noise/crosstalk (coffee machine) --
[06:45] Dana Chen: small ask — can you annotate which rows in CSV correspond to kernel compile spikes so my SREs can filter?
[06:52] Marco Ruiz: yes we'll add "compile_flag" column and a note in the README.
[06:57] Priyanka Patel: timeline-wise, when can we expect the retest CSVs?
[07:02] Jordan Lee: SE runs take about 24-48 hours depending on queue. Priya, estimate?
[07:06] Priya Nair: I'll spin up runs today; expect preliminary CSV by 2027-11-06.
[07:11] Rajiv Kapoor: on compliance, send SOC2 and KMS diagrams. we need to review before any Dedicated commitment.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: will send SOC2 pack and a Private deployment checklist.
[07:22] Miguel Santos: another observation — IncumbentAI seems to have a sticky cache for certain prompt families. did you test prefix caching?
[07:30] Priya Nair: we've been testing prefix/KV caching; for some prompts with heavy repetition it's very effective. the trick is cache key stability across different user tokens.
[07:41] Dana Chen: ok let's make sure the 2k prompt set includes those repeat patterns.
[07:45] Miguel Santos: will do.
[07:48] Jordan Lee: ok, let's capture the exact experiment matrix agreed:
[07:52] Jordan Lee: 1) latency-first pinned fp16 with batch_wait_ms=5, KV prewarm
[07:59] Jordan Lee: 2) latency-first pinned q4f with batch_wait_ms=5, KV prewarm
[08:05] Jordan Lee: 3) cost-first with fallback q4f, batch_wait_ms=30, KV default
[08:11] Jordan Lee: 4) latency-first fp16 with KV disabled (isolation run)
[08:17] Priya Nair: will run each at least 10k requests or 30 minutes steady-state, whichever hits first. we'll capture median, p50/p95/p99, kernel-compile counts, queue time, request hop, and token breakdown.
[08:30] Priyanka Patel: are you able to tag results in CRM with a link to the raw Grafana dashboards?
[08:35] Marco Ruiz: yes we will provide dashboard snapshots and a public read-only link.
[08:40] Dana Chen: one more question on expected ramp if we move to Dedicated — how quickly can we get a slot? we might want it mid-November.
[08:49] Jordan Lee: Dedicated provisioning typically 7-14 days after PO, but we can provide temporary priority for POC runs to accelerate.
[08:58] Miguel Santos: chase — will custom quantization (post-training) help? we have some LUT patterns in our models.
[09:04] Priya Nair: we support tuned quantization profiles; that takes a little more time but can reduce jitter. we can roadmap that after these routing tests.
[09:14] Dana Chen: ok, sounds good. recap and owners?
[09:19] Jordan Lee: recap — Priya runs experiment matrix and shares CSVs by 2027-11-06; Miguel uploads prompts and trace by 2027-11-05; Jordan shares pricing and SOC2 package by 2027-11-04; schedule SRE deep-dive for week of 2027-11-08.
[09:33] Priya Nair: and action item, I'll include compile flags and per-request kernel timing.
[09:40] Rajiv Kapoor: thanks everyone I think that's clear.
[09:45] Jordan Lee: great — thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the SRE deep-dive.
[09:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear of product names (Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedicatd) and KV cache spelled inconsistently as "kv cash" in some snippets.
